feature: Bring in a second clip and cut between clips
summary: Drag a video or a sound from the Finder onto the timeline and it lands at the moment and on the track under the pointer: it covers what was there, or with the command key held it pushes what comes after along. Clips that meet on a track have an edit point you can pick.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open a screen recording and keep the timeline open.

try.do: Drag a second video from the Finder over V1, near the end of the recording, and hold it there.
Let go. It butts onto the end of the recording on V1, in the second clip colour.
Drag a third video to the end of that one and let go.
Drag a music file over V1 about four seconds in, with the playhead somewhere else, and let go.
Hold the command key and drag another video into the middle of the recording.
Let go. The recording splits round it and everything after moves along.
Click exactly on the join between two clips.
Press Command Z, then drop the music on the picture instead of the timeline.

evaluate: Does the dashed ghost show you where the clip will land before you let go, including past the end?
Is overwrite by default and command for insert what your hands expect from Premiere?
Is the snap onto the end of the clip before strong enough, or do you still leave slivers of black?
Is a sound dropped over a picture track going to the Audio track what you expected, or should it refuse?
Is the edit point easy to hit without grabbing the trim edge of the clip beside it?
rough: A clip's own sound still rides inside its bar (the white line through the picture clips) rather than on its own segment under it. That is the next task, A clip's sound is on the timeline from the moment it opens, and it now covers dropped clips and split halves too.

The Library shelf holds pictures only, so the mock's drag a b-roll tile from the Library is not possible yet. Filed as p1: Recordings and sounds in a document sit on the Library shelf and drag onto the timeline.
Picking an edit point shows no edit point properties and no transition picker yet; that is Click a cut and pick a transition from tiles.
The timeline makes room past its end while a file is in the air, so the lanes shrink once as the file arrives. Premiere keeps empty timeline past the end all the time instead.
An insert shows where the clip goes in but does not preview everything after it moving along; it moves when you let go.

Mock differences: video.html lights the whole lane with a dashed edge while something is over it; this draws a ghost the length of the clip instead, which says more. The edit point follows comp-video.html's CSS (faint hairline at rest, amber on hover, amber ring when picked).
